drivers: one small library called in-process by the host (task.md asks for one Python module, unified/billing.py)
strong consistency: an order, its ledger entry and its processed webhook id must change together or not at all
money movement must be exactly-once, which is far simpler inside one transaction boundary
no independent scaling, team or release need

alternatives.reason: splitting orders, payments and ledger across services turns every state change into a distributed transaction, the opposite of the exactly-once requirement
webhooks are events, but they are handled synchronously with an event-id dedupe; a message bus adds eventual consistency and infrastructure nothing here needs
there is no existing system that must stay separate; the gateway is already behind an adapter
no part has different needs from the rest

style.reason: The simplest design that gives one atomic write per state change and one place that decides each order's state

stack.backend: an in-process library: unified/billing.py exposing create_app(gateway, store=None)
stack.database: an in-memory store with atomic batch writes behind a small interface (MemoryStore); a real database adapter would implement the same write(ops) contract
stack.gateway: the injected gateway object (gateway.FakeGateway in tests) behind a gateway-adapter section

reasons.language: D01: the user asked for a Python module and no package installs are approved; the mock gateway is Python
reasons.backend: D02: the API in task.md is a Python object API, so no HTTP layer is built
reasons.database: D04: task.md's store contract (fail_next_write, StoreError) needs one write per state change; no database package may be installed
reasons.tests: D01: unittest needs no install and run_tests.py has a built-in unittest harness

modules.name: store
modules.responsibility: Atomic batch writes of order, ledger, event, key and renewal records; raises StoreError and applies nothing when a write fails (fail_next_write)

modules.name: gateway-adapter
modules.responsibility: Calls the injected gateway's charge(amount_cents, key) and refund(charge_id); recognises timeouts

modules.name: orders
modules.responsibility: Create and read orders; the status transition table every change goes through

modules.name: ledger
modules.responsibility: Ledger entries for charges and refunds, added inside the same write as the order change

modules.name: payments
modules.responsibility: pay(order_id, key): key binding, attempt key written before the call, timeout retry with the same key, paid state written atomically

modules.name: refunds
modules.responsibility: cancel(order_id): cancel a pending order, or refund a paid one exactly once (refund intent written first)

modules.name: webhooks
modules.responsibility: handle_webhook(event): event-id dedupe in the same write as the effect; charge.succeeded and charge.refunded

modules.name: subscriptions
modules.responsibility: renew(subscription, period): one order per subscription per period

modules.name: facade
modules.responsibility: create_app() and the BillingApp object: the public API from task.md, one lock around every operation

entities.name: Order
entities.primary_key: id: text 'ord_<n>', generated by the app
entities.notes: A's paid flag is not stored: paid means status == 'paid' (resolution database:field-meaning:order-payment-state); charge_id, attempt_key, refund_state, refund_id are nullable; amount_cents > 0; status in (pending, paid, cancelled, refunded); refund_state in (requested, done)

entities.name: IdempotencyKey
entities.notes: binds each client key to one order (resolution charge-idempotency)

entities.name: WebhookEvent
entities.notes: processed event ids, written in the same write as the event's effect

entities.name: Renewal
entities.notes: B's subscription is passed in by the caller; the app records one renewal per period

auth.method: none: an in-process library; the host application authenticates its callers

configuration.note: no settings: the gateway and store are passed to create_app; no secrets

slices.name: Core loop: create an order, pay it once, see the ledger

decisions.decision: Python 3 standard library only; tests with unittest
decisions.reason: the user asked for a Python module; installing packages is not approved

decisions.decision: Modular monolith in a single file, unified/billing.py, with one section per module
decisions.reason: task.md fixes the module path; a single file imports the same way whether loaded as unified.billing or by path; module boundaries are kept as sections with one-way dependencies

decisions.decision: One Order with a single status field and an enforced transition table

Store contract: write(ops) applies a batch atomically or raises StoreError and applies nothing; it honours fail_next_write on the store passed in (resetting it after one failure); create_app(gateway) without a store makes a MemoryStore
decisions.reason: resolution database:atomicity:write-failure and the store contract in task.md

decisions.decision: Intent before gateway calls: the attempt key (pay) or the refund intent (cancel) is written before the gateway is called
decisions.reason: a failed write must never leave a charge or refund without a record

decisions.decision: Gateway timeout: recognised by exception class name GatewayTimeout (or TimeoutError), retried once with the same key; otherwise the order stays pending and the error is raised
decisions.reason: resolution application:business-rule:gateway-timeout; matching by name avoids importing the test's gateway module from a fixed path

decisions.decision: Cancelling a paid order ends in status 'refunded'; a charge.succeeded for an order cancelled while its payment was in doubt is refunded at once and the order ends 'refunded'
decisions.reason: resolution application:workflow:cancel-paid-order; money taken on a cancelled order must go back

decisions.decision: A refund whose gateway outcome is unknown stays refund_state 'requested'; it is never re-sent automatically; cancel raises RefundPending and the charge.refunded webhook completes it
decisions.reason: the gateway's refund is not idempotent, so re-sending could refund twice

decisions.decision: No HTTP API, no auth, no UI: the Python object API in task.md is the interface
decisions.reason: task.md defines the API; adding layers nobody asked for adds risk
